title: Real-world robot control by deep active inference with a temporally hierarchical world model
core_idea: Propose a deep active inference framework for real-world robot control that separates representation into a world model encoding slow and fast hidden-state dynamics and an action model that compresses action sequences into a learned set of abstract actions via vector quantization. An abstract world model predicts future slow states conditioned on abstract actions, enabling low-cost action selection that supports both goal-directed and exploratory behaviors under environmental uncertainty while aiming to reduce computational cost.
tldr: A hierarchical deep active inference setup that abstracts states and actions (via temporal scales and vector quantization) to enable efficient, low-cost planning for goal-directed and exploratory robot control in uncertain real-world environments.
